purpose: Omeprazole is used to reduce the amount of acid your stomach makes. It helps treat conditions like heartburn, acid reflux, stomach ulcers, and a condition called GERD (gastroesophageal reflux disease). It can also help protect your stomach if you are taking certain pain medicines like ibuprofen.
how_it_works: Your stomach has tiny pumps that produce acid to help digest food. Omeprazole works by blocking these pumps so they make much less acid. With less acid in your stomach, your symptoms like burning, pain, and irritation have a chance to heal and feel better.
common_side_effects: Most people tolerate this medicine well, but some may experience headache, nausea, stomach pain, diarrhea, or constipation. Some people notice gas or an upset stomach when they first start taking it. These effects are usually mild and often go away on their own.
warnings: Taking omeprazole for a long time (more than a year) may lower your magnesium and vitamin B12 levels, so your doctor may check these with a blood test. Long-term use has also been linked to a slightly higher risk of bone fractures, so talk to your doctor if you have concerns about bone health. Let your doctor know if your symptoms do not improve after 2 to 4 weeks, or if you have trouble swallowing or notice unexplained weight loss.
typical_dosing: The usual dose for adults is 20 mg taken once a day, about 30 to 60 minutes before a meal — breakfast is usually the best time. Your doctor may prescribe a higher dose (40 mg) depending on your condition. For over-the-counter heartburn treatment, it is typically taken once daily for 14 days, and you should not use it for more than 14 days without talking to your doctor.
